title: LAN pairing with PAKE and device trust
goal: Pair a guest with a LAN host using a short code and a real PAKE (CPace over ristretto255), so a wrong or eavesdropped code never yields the session key, and remember trusted devices with TOFU for reconnects.
scope_in: Pairing code: 8 characters from the alphabet `A-Z` and `2-9` without `0 O 1 I L` (shown `ABCD-EFGH`), CSPRNG-generated, valid 5 minutes, one successful use per guest, at most 5 attempts per code.

CPace (draft-irtf-cfrg-cpace, ristretto255 + SHA-512, libsodium via the C056 wrapper) with channel identifiers = host session id and both device fingerprints; derive `ISK`; exchange key-confirmation MACs; constant-time verification.

Wire messages `lan.pair.1`..`lan.pair.4` and `lan.pair.err {code}` exactly as in schemas/lan-pair.schema.json (guest: `cpace_msg`, device {id,x25519,ed25519,name}, fp; host: `cpace_msg`, device, fp; guest `confirm`; host `confirm`, `ok:true`, member, session {sid,name,policy}), validated at the boundary.
Host-side `HostPairing` state machine per connection and guest-side `GuestPairing`, both transport-agnostic over a `TextChannel` interface; host implements the `PairingHandler` expected by lane C072.

Failure policy: wrong code -> `lan.pair.err {code:'bad_code'}` then close 4403; 5 failed attempts for a code -> code invalidated; a source IP with repeated failures is banned for 10 minutes (`BanList`).

After success: trust store entries (device id -> x25519/ed25519, fingerprint) kept for the session lifetime; a 256-bit per-session reconnect token issued in `lan.pair.4`, stored in memory and (guest side) in the keychain, validated later via `TokenValidator` so reconnects skip pairing; after confirmation, emit `paired` with the guest's keys so the engine can send the sealed `key.grant` (grant creation itself is lane C056/C057 territory).
scope_out: Session key grants and encryption: lane C056 (and the host engine lane C075 sending `key.grant`).
The WebSocket server and sequencing: lane C072. mDNS: lane C071. UI for showing/entering the code and fingerprint comparison: TUI lanes.
Internet-scale PAKE or account-based trust: not in v1.
build_against: Pure library over an in-memory `TextChannel` pair; no sockets, no backend. Test vectors: the CPace draft's ristretto255 appendix vectors plus the lan.pair fixtures in contracts/fixtures/lan/ (valid run, wrong code, replayed message, truncated message); device keys from lane C056's test helpers.
interfaces: `generatePairingCode(rng?: () => Uint8Array): { code: string /* 'ABCDEFGH' */; display: string /* 'ABCD-EFGH' */ }`; `normalizeCode(input: string): string | null`

`class HostPairing implements PairingHandler { constructor(o: { sessionId: string; sessionName: string; policy: SessionPolicy; device: DeviceKeyStore; fingerprint: string; clock; bans: MutableBanList; trust: PairingTrustStore }); openCode(ttlMs?: number /*300000*/): { display: string; expiresAt: string }; on('paired', (g: { memberHint: string; device: { id: string; x25519: string; ed25519: string; name: string }; reconnectToken: string }) => void); on('failed', (f: { ip: string; reason: 'bad_code'|'expired'|'too_many'|'protocol' }) => void) }`

`guestPair(o: { channel: TextChannel; code: string; device: DeviceKeyStore; hostSessionId?: string; expectedFingerprint?: string; clock }): Promise<{ member: MemberInfo; session: { sid: string; name: string; policy: SessionPolicy }; hostDevice: DeviceRecord; reconnectToken: string }>`
`interface TextChannel { send(text: string): void; onMessage(fn: (text: string) => void): void; onClose(fn: (code: number) => void): void; close(code: number): void }`
`class ReconnectTokens { issue(deviceId: string): string; validate(token: string, remoteIp: string): { deviceId: string } | null; revoke(deviceId: string): void }` implementing `TokenValidator`
`interface PairingTrustStore { remember(d: DeviceRecord): void; get(id: string): DeviceRecord | null }`
acceptance: Generated codes are exactly 8 characters from the 31-character alphabet, never contain 0, O, 1, I or L, and 10 000 samples show a roughly uniform distribution (chi-square p > 0.001); `normalizeCode('abcd-efgh')` returns `ABCDEFGH`; characters outside the alphabet return null.

Correct code: guest and host complete lan.pair.1-4 over the in-memory channel, derive equal `ISK`, both confirmations verify, host emits `paired` with the guest's device keys, and the guest receives a 256-bit (43-char base64url) reconnect token.

Wrong code: the host sends `lan.pair.err {code:'bad_code'}` and closes 4403; no confirmation MAC is revealed; the same ISK is never derived (assert different ISK values / failed confirmation on both sides).

After 5 failed attempts on one code, the 6th attempt with the CORRECT code is rejected (code invalidated); the source IP is on the BanList and `isBanned(ip)` is true for 10 minutes and false after 10 min + 1 s (fake clock).
A code is valid for 5 minutes: at 5 min + 1 s a correct code fails with `expired`; a second guest using an already-consumed code fails (one use per guest).
CPace known-answer test from the draft's ristretto255 appendix produces the expected `ISK` for the fixed inputs; replaying a recorded `lan.pair.1` against a fresh host state fails confirmation.

Channel binding: a MITM that relays messages between a guest and host with different fingerprints/session ids in the transcript causes confirmation failure; if `expectedFingerprint` (from mDNS) differs from the host's actual `fp`, `guestPair` rejects with `FingerprintMismatchError` before sending confirmation.
Reconnect: `validate(token, ip)` accepts a valid token once per connection attempt and rejects tokens after `revoke`, after session end, and tokens with one flipped bit; comparison is constant-time.

Messages that fail the lan-pair schema (missing `cpace_msg`, wrong lengths, extra huge field > 4 KiB) are rejected with `protocol` failure without throwing; fuzz of 10 000 random messages never crashes.
No log line or error contains the code, ISK, confirmation MACs or token; the trust store keeps only public keys and fingerprints.
tests: pairing/code.test.ts: alphabet, uniformity, normalisation, expiry, attempt counting.
pairing/cpace.test.ts: draft known-answer vectors, wrong-password divergence, invalid group element rejection (identity point, non-canonical encoding).
pairing/flow.test.ts: full 4-message flow, wrong code, replay, reordering, truncation, timeouts.
pairing/ban.test.ts: 5-attempt limit and 10-minute IP ban on a fake clock.
pairing/tokens.test.ts: issue/validate/revoke, constant-time path, persistence of guest token in keychain fake.
pairing/redaction.test.ts: secrets never in logs or errors.
guardrails: MUST use CPace (balanced PAKE) over ristretto255 with libsodium; MUST NOT send the code or a hash of it, MUST NOT implement a home-made PAKE, and MUST reject identity/low-order group elements and non-canonical encodings.
MUST bind the exchange to the host session id and BOTH device fingerprints and MUST verify key-confirmation MACs in constant time before trusting the peer or issuing any key grant.
MUST enforce: code TTL 5 minutes, one use per guest, 5 attempts per code, 10-minute IP ban after repeated failure; counters live on the host and survive reconnects of the same socket.
MUST NOT log, display in errors or persist the pairing code, ISK, MACs or reconnect tokens; the code is shown only by the host UI and kept in memory.
MUST generate codes and tokens from the platform CSPRNG and tokens as >= 256 bits; MUST store the guest-side token only in the OS keychain (and memory).
MUST treat a changed key for an already-trusted device id as a warning result (TOFU violation), never a silent overwrite.
MUST NOT send `key.grant` itself; it only signals `paired` after successful confirmation.
failure_modes: Guest disconnects mid-handshake -> the half-open state is discarded after 10 s; the attempt counts as failed only if a `lan.pair.3` with a bad confirm was received.
Clock change during code validity -> expiry uses a monotonic clock; a backwards jump never extends validity.
Fingerprint from mDNS disagrees with the one in lan.pair.2 -> abort with FingerprintMismatchError and tell the user to verify out of band.
Host restarted -> reconnect tokens are invalid (session ended); guests must pair again with a new code.
notes: CONTRACT GAP: CT-LAN names CPace but not the ciphersuite id, domain-separation strings, channel-identifier concatenation order, the exact `ISK` derivation input or the confirmation MAC construction (BLAKE2b keyed vs HMAC); this card follows CPACE-RISTR255-SHA512 from the IRTF draft and needs fixtures in contracts/fixtures/lan/ to be pinned in a Contract PR. Also: libsodium-wrappers (non-sumo) may lack some ristretto255 helpers; confirm with lane C056 whether the sumo build is required.
